note: Which one should I pick? Side-by-side cards for AWS services people mix up (src/ui/CompareCard.tsx). Facts from the AWS decision guides and each service's own docs (`source`); the wording is ours.

comparisons.title: SQS or EventBridge?
comparisons.simple: A queue holds work until a worker takes it. An event bus sends each event to every rule that wants it.

options.pick: Pick it when a worker should take jobs at its own pace, and no job may get lost.
Pick it when many services react to the same event, chosen by rules on what's in it.

values.eventbridge: No: retries delivery for up to 24 hours
Rich pattern matching on the content

comparisons.title: ECS, EKS or Fargate?
comparisons.simple: ECS and EKS decide where your containers run. Fargate is the engine that runs them, with no servers to manage.

options.pick: Pick it for the simplest AWS-native way to run containers, with tight IAM and VPC integration.
Pick it when your team already uses Kubernetes, or the app must stay portable to it.
Pick it under ECS or EKS when you don't want to patch or scale any servers.

values.fargate: Just the task's CPU and memory

comparisons.title: S3, EBS or EFS?
comparisons.simple: EBS is one server's own disk. EFS is a shared folder for many servers. S3 is endless storage you reach by web calls.

options.pick: Pick it for a database or boot disk on one EC2 instance that needs fast, steady disk speed.
Pick it when many servers or containers must read and write the same files at once.
Pick it for files, backups, websites and data lakes: any amount, read over the internet.

comparisons.title: RDS, Aurora or DynamoDB?
comparisons.simple: RDS and Aurora are tables you query with SQL. DynamoDB is a key-value store that stays fast at any size.

options.pick: Pick it to run a familiar engine (MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle…) without managing it.
Pick it for MySQL or PostgreSQL that needs more speed, read replicas and fast failover.
Pick it when you look items up by key, need huge scale, and want nothing to run.

comparisons.title: EC2, Lambda or Fargate?
comparisons.simple: EC2 is a whole server you run. Lambda runs a function for each event. Fargate runs containers with no servers.

options.pick: Pick it when you need full control of the machine, or software that must run all the time.
Pick it for short, event-driven code (up to 15 minutes), paying only while it runs.
Pick it for long-running containers when you don't want to manage the servers under them.

values.fargate: The task's CPU and memory while it runs

comparisons.title: Athena, Redshift or Glue?
comparisons.simple: Glue gets data ready. Athena asks questions of files in S3. Redshift is a warehouse built for big repeated reports.

options.pick: Pick it to query files in S3 with SQL right away, paying per data scanned.
Pick it for dashboards and reports that run all day over very large, organised data.
Pick it to catalogue, clean and move data (ETL) so the others can query it.

comparisons.title: IAM or Cognito?
comparisons.simple: IAM decides what your team and your code may do in AWS. Cognito signs in the users of your own app.

options.pick: Pick it for permissions inside AWS: people, roles and services calling AWS APIs.
Pick it for your app's own sign-up and sign-in, including social and enterprise logins.

values.iam: Your team, apps and AWS services

comparisons.title: Shield or GuardDuty?
comparisons.simple: Shield blocks floods of traffic meant to knock you offline. GuardDuty watches your account for signs of an attack.

options.pick: Pick it (Standard is on for free) to protect your app from DDoS floods.
Pick it to spot stolen keys, crypto mining or odd access from your logs.

values.guardduty: Analyses logs (CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, DNS)
Turn it on, act on findings

comparisons.title: Bedrock, SageMaker AI or Amazon Q?
comparisons.simple: Bedrock lends you ready AI models to build with. SageMaker AI builds your own. Q is an assistant ready to use.

options.pick: Pick it to build an app on top of foundation models through one API, with no servers.
Pick it to train, tune and host your own machine learning models.
Pick it when you want a ready-made AI assistant for AWS work, not to build one.

comparisons.title: ElastiCache or DynamoDB?
comparisons.simple: ElastiCache keeps hot data in memory for speed. DynamoDB is the durable database that data comes from.

options.pick: Pick it in front of a database to answer repeated reads in microseconds.
Pick it as the system of record: data that must never be lost.

comparisons.title: Lambda Managed Instances or EC2?
comparisons.simple: Managed Instances runs Lambda functions on EC2 servers that Lambda looks after. Plain EC2 leaves the upkeep to you.

options.pick: Pick it for steady, heavy traffic in Lambda's model, with Lambda patching and scaling the servers.
Pick it when you need full control of the machine and its software, all the time.

values.lambda: Automatic on CPU use, no cold starts
Savings Plans cover the EC2 part

comparisons.title: Cognito, API Gateway or IAM for tenants?
comparisons.simple: Cognito knows which tenant a user is, API Gateway checks every call, and IAM limits what the code may touch.

options.pick: Pick it to sign users in and stamp each one with a tenant they can't change themselves.
Pick it to check every request at the door and pass the caller's tenant on to your code.
Pick it to limit each request's keys to one tenant's rows, so a bug can't cross over.

values.cognito: Who the user is, and their tenant
values.apigateway: Let each call in, or not
values.iam: What the code may read and write

values.apigateway: A Lambda authorizer returns a policy and context
Usage plans throttle each key (best effort)

comparisons.title: Neptune or DynamoDB?
comparisons.simple: DynamoDB fetches items by their key, fast, for millions of users. Neptune follows the links between things.

options.pick: Pick it for huge numbers of quick lookups by key, like sessions or shopping carts.
Pick it when the links matter most: social networks, fraud rings or recommendations.

values.neptune: Graph: things and the links between them

values.dynamodb: Single-digit millisecond reads at any scale
values.neptune: Following many links and spotting patterns fast

comparisons.title: Rekognition or Textract?
comparisons.simple: Rekognition says what's in a photo or video. Textract reads documents and keeps their tables and forms.

options.pick: Pick it to find objects, faces, unsafe content or words in photos and videos.
Pick it to pull text, tables and form fields out of scanned pages, forms and files.

values.textract: Printed and handwritten text, tables, form fields

values.rekognition: Text it spots in a picture
values.textract: Text with its structure and reading order

values.rekognition: Custom Labels for your own objects

comparisons.title: Elastic Beanstalk, ECS or Lambda?
comparisons.simple: Beanstalk runs your web app's code on servers it sets up. ECS runs containers. Lambda runs code only when events arrive.

options.pick: Pick it to deploy a web app quickly from code, with AWS setting up servers and scaling.
Pick it when your app is already packed in containers and runs all the time.
Pick it for short jobs that run when something happens, with no servers at all.

values.beanstalk: Your code, or a Docker image
None: you pay for what it creates
values.ecs: None: you pay for EC2 or Fargate

comparisons.title: CloudWatch, GuardDuty or Security Agent?
comparisons.simple: CloudWatch watches health and logs actions. GuardDuty spots attacks. Security Agent attacks your own app as a test.

options.pick: Pick it to see how things run, get alarms, and keep an audit trail with CloudTrail.
Pick it to be warned of attacks or misuse in your account, always on.
Pick it before a release, to find weak spots with an authorised practice attack.

values.cloudwatch: Metrics, logs, alarms; CloudTrail logs actions
values.securityagent: Penetration tests on your own app
Proven findings with steps to fix

comparisons.title: CloudFront or Route 53?
comparisons.simple: Route 53 tells browsers where your site lives. CloudFront serves it from a place near each visitor.

options.pick: Pick it to make a site load faster everywhere by keeping copies near your users.
Pick it to point your domain name at your app, and send users to a healthy copy.

values.cloudfront: Content delivery network: caches and serves content
values.route53: Domain Name System: turns names into addresses
Latency routing to the quickest Region

values.cloudfront: Together: Route 53 points your name at CloudFront
values.route53: Together: an alias record to the distribution

comparisons.title: KMS or IAM?
comparisons.simple: IAM decides who may do what in AWS. KMS holds the keys that lock your data, and decides who may use each key.

options.pick: Pick it to give people and apps only the access to AWS they need.
Pick it to encrypt data with keys you control, and see each time a key is used.

values.iam: Who can call which AWS action on what
values.kms: Who can use each encryption key

values.iam: Policies on users, roles and resources
values.kms: One key policy per key, plus IAM if it allows
Monthly fee per key you create, plus requests

comparisons.title: Lake Formation or IAM for a data lake?
comparisons.simple: IAM opens the door to the lake's services. Lake Formation decides which tables, columns and rows each person sees.

options.pick: Pick it to grant people just some tables, columns or rows, like in a database.
Pick it for broad access: who may use Lake Formation, Glue and the other services at all.

values.lakeformation: Fine-grained: what each person can read
values.iam: Coarse-grained: which services they can call

comparisons.title: VPC rules or AWS WAF?
comparisons.simple: Your VPC's security groups and network rules decide which addresses and ports get in. AWS WAF reads each web request.

options.pick: Pick it to keep resources private and allow only the addresses and ports they need.
Pick it to block bad web requests, like injection attacks or floods, before your app.

values.shield: The content of each web request

values.vpc: Security groups, network ACLs, private subnets
values.shield: AWS WAF rules, Shield for DDoS
Websites and APIs: CloudFront, load balancers, API Gateway

comparisons.title: AgentCore or Bedrock?
comparisons.simple: Bedrock gives you the AI models. AgentCore runs the agents built on them, with memory, tools and safe sessions.

options.pick: Pick it to call foundation models from your app, with knowledge bases and guardrails.
Pick it to deploy and run agents in production, with any framework and any model.

values.agentcore: A platform to run and operate agents

values.bedrock: From Amazon and other AI companies
values.agentcore: Any model, in or outside Bedrock

comparisons.title: App Runner or ECS Express Mode?
comparisons.simple: Both turn one container image into a running website. App Runner takes no new customers, so new apps use Express Mode.

options.pick: Pick it only if your team already runs apps on it: it's closed to new customers.
Pick it (Express Mode) for a new web app from one container image, with AWS building the stack.

values.apprunner: Source code or a container image
values.ecs: A container image (add a build step for code)
Your account: Fargate, a load balancer, scaling

values.apprunner: Compute by the second, plus deployment and build fees
values.ecs: None beyond the resources it creates

comparisons.title: Batch or Lambda?
comparisons.simple: Lambda runs short bits of code the moment something happens. Batch queues long jobs and runs them on capacity it scales.

options.pick: Pick it for long, heavy jobs, like rendering or simulations, that can wait in a queue.
Pick it for short tasks, up to 15 minutes each, that run as soon as an event happens.

values.batch: As long as the job needs
When capacity fits the queued job
Containers on EC2, Spot or Fargate
None: you pay for the compute

comparisons.title: Lightsail, Beanstalk or EC2?
comparisons.simple: Lightsail is all-in-one for a fixed price. Beanstalk runs your code and handles servers. EC2 gives full control.

options.pick: Pick it for a simple site or blog at a fixed, predictable monthly price, with little setup.
Pick it to upload your code and let AWS handle the servers, scaling and health checks.
Pick it when you need full control of the server, the network and the pricing options.

values.beanstalk: No extra charge: pay for what it creates
values.ec2: Pay per use, or commit for less
You set up and manage it all

values.lightsail: Simple: a range of plan sizes

comparisons.title: AWS Backup or EBS snapshots on their own?
comparisons.simple: Data Lifecycle Manager schedules snapshots of EC2 disks. AWS Backup runs one plan across many services.

options.pick: Pick it for one backup plan across many services, with locked vaults and copies to other accounts.
Pick it when you only need scheduled snapshots of EC2 disks, with Data Lifecycle Manager.

values.backup: EC2, EBS, S3, DynamoDB, RDS, EFS and more

values.ebs: Not part of Data Lifecycle Manager

comparisons.title: Kinesis or SQS?
comparisons.simple: A queue hands each message to one worker. A stream keeps every record in order, so many readers can each read it all.

options.pick: Pick it when many apps must read the same records, in order, and maybe read them again.
Pick it when each job should go to one worker, at its own pace, then be deleted.

values.sqs: Each message goes to one consumer

comparisons.title: OpenSearch or DynamoDB?
comparisons.simple: DynamoDB finds an item when you know its key. OpenSearch finds items by any words inside them.

options.pick: Pick it to store items and fetch each one fast by its key, at any scale.
Pick it to search text by any word, analyse logs, or find similar items with vector search.

values.dynamodb: Primary key, or an index you add
values.opensearch: Any word or field in the documents

values.dynamodb: Fast reads and writes at any scale
values.opensearch: Search, log analytics and vector search

comparisons.title: DocumentDB or DynamoDB?
comparisons.simple: DynamoDB fetches items by key, fast, at any scale. DocumentDB stores rich documents you can query by any field.

options.pick: Pick it for huge numbers of quick reads and writes by key, like sessions or shopping carts.
Pick it for documents you query in rich ways, or apps already built with MongoDB drivers.

values.dynamodb: Single-digit millisecond reads at any scale
values.documentdb: Rich queries across any field of a document

comparisons.title: VPC peering or Transit Gateway?
comparisons.simple: Peering joins two networks directly. A transit gateway is one hub that every network plugs into.

options.pick: Pick it (VPC peering) to link a few VPCs in pairs, with nothing in between.
Pick it when many VPCs, accounts and office links must reach each other through one hub.

values.vpc: Direct links between pairs of VPCs

values.transitgateway: Yes, as its route tables allow

values.vpc: Can't share one VPC's VPN or gateway
values.transitgateway: VPN and Direct Connect attach to the hub

values.vpc: Only peer the pairs that may talk

comparisons.title: CloudFront or Global Accelerator?
comparisons.simple: CloudFront keeps copies of web content near people. Global Accelerator carries any traffic fast to your app's Regions.

options.pick: Pick it to make websites, images, videos and APIs faster for people around the world.
Pick it for fixed IP addresses, fast Region failover, or traffic that isn't web pages, like games.

values.cloudfront: Caches and delivers web content at the edge
values.globalaccelerator: Carries traffic over the AWS network to your Regions
Gaming, IoT, voice calls, fixed-address apps

comparisons.title: Secrets Manager or KMS?
comparisons.simple: KMS makes and guards the keys that lock data. Secrets Manager stores passwords and API keys and changes them.

options.pick: Pick it to keep database passwords, API keys and tokens out of code, and rotate them.
Pick it to create and control the keys that encrypt your data, in AWS services or your app.

values.secretsmanager: The secret value, at run time
values.kms: Encrypt and decrypt results; the key never leaves

values.secretsmanager: Changes the secret on your schedule
values.kms: New key material yearly by default

comparisons.title: GuardDuty, Inspector or Macie?
comparisons.simple: GuardDuty spots attackers, Inspector finds known software flaws, and Macie finds sensitive data left in buckets.

options.pick: Pick it to be warned of attacks or misuse in your account, from its logs.
Pick it to find known flaws and open network paths on servers, images and functions.
Pick it to find personal or secret data in S3, and buckets left open.

values.guardduty: Logs: CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, DNS

values.macie: Sensitive data and risky bucket settings

comparisons.title: Macie or Comprehend for personal data?
comparisons.simple: Macie hunts for personal data stored in your S3 buckets. Comprehend finds and hides it in text your app handles.

options.pick: Pick it to discover where sensitive data sits in S3 and which buckets are exposed.
Pick it to detect or redact personal details in text as part of your own pipeline.

values.comprehend: Personal details like addresses and phone numbers
Returns locations, or a redacted copy

comparisons.title: GuardDuty or Security Hub?
comparisons.simple: GuardDuty is one watcher that finds threats. Security Hub puts every watcher's findings on one board.

options.pick: Pick it to detect threats like stolen keys or crypto mining from your logs.
Pick it to see, rank and act on findings from all your security services in one place.

comparisons.title: Polly, Comprehend or Textract?
comparisons.simple: Textract reads scanned pages, Comprehend works out what text means, and Polly reads text aloud.

options.pick: Pick it to turn text into natural speech for apps, games or accessibility.
Pick it to find the mood, names, key phrases and personal data in typed text.
Pick it to pull text, tables and form fields out of scanned pages and documents.

values.polly: Background task saves audio to S3
values.comprehend: Asynchronous jobs on files in S3

comparisons.title: Step Functions or EventBridge?
comparisons.simple: Step Functions conducts the steps of one job in order. EventBridge passes news of events on to whoever cares.

options.pick: Pick it to run a job's steps in order, with branches, retries and waits.
Pick it to route events between services, or to run things on a schedule.

values.stepfunctions: Workflows: one conductor runs the steps
values.eventbridge: Events: senders and listeners stay apart

values.stepfunctions: Business processes, data pipelines, microservice coordination
Order, branches, parallel steps, retries and errors
values.eventbridge: Matching events to rules and delivering them

comparisons.title: CloudFormation or Systems Manager?
comparisons.simple: CloudFormation builds your resources from a blueprint. Systems Manager looks after the servers once they run.

options.pick: Pick it to create, update and delete resources together from a template.
Pick it to patch, run commands on and connect to servers you already have.

values.cloudformation: A template and the stack built from it
values.systemsmanager: Managed nodes running the SSM Agent

values.cloudformation: Build the same setup in every Region
values.systemsmanager: Patch every server on Tuesday night

comparisons.title: Organizations or Config?
comparisons.simple: Organizations sets limits accounts cannot cross. Config checks how things are set up and flags what breaks your rules.

options.pick: Pick it to group accounts and set guardrails, like SCPs, that stop actions before they happen.
Pick it to record settings over time, check them against rules and fix what breaks them.

values.organizations: Prevents: caps what accounts can do
values.config: Detects: flags resources that break rules

values.organizations: The action is stopped before it happens

comparisons.title: AppSync or API Gateway?
comparisons.simple: AppSync gives apps one GraphQL endpoint to ask many sources at once. API Gateway runs classic web APIs, one route each.

options.pick: Pick it for GraphQL: one request for exactly the fields an app needs, with live updates.
Pick it for classic web APIs and WebSocket APIs in front of your services.

values.appsync: One endpoint for many data sources
values.apigateway: One route per resource or action
